questions.prompt: Put the six troubleshooting steps in order.
items: Establish a theory of probable cause
Plan and carry out the fix
questions.explanation: Gather information first, test theories one at a time, and always finish by verifying and documenting.

questions.prompt: A user says their computer "stopped working" this morning. What should you do first?
choices: Ask what happens exactly and what changed recently
questions.explanation: Identify the problem before changing anything. What changed recently is often the cause.

questions.prompt: Your first theory turns out to be wrong. What next?
choices: Go back and establish a new theory
questions.explanation: If a theory is not confirmed, return to step 2 and test the next most likely cause.

questions.prompt: Which belong in your documentation? Select all that apply.
choices: What you did to fix it
questions.explanation: Record symptoms, cause, actions and result. Never record passwords.

questions.prompt: Why should you test the simplest causes first?
choices: They are usually the most expensive
They are common, quick to check and rule out
questions.explanation: Loose cables, switches and recent changes cause many faults and take seconds to check.
